title: Anticipatory Residency Controller for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Dedicated customer fleets occasionally see throughput regressions after scale events or tenant churn because model weights are not resident and KV caches are cold. Existing warm-pool efforts focus on naive prefetching and full-weight replication which is either wasteful or slow to adapt to traffic patterns. Goal: build an Anticipatory Residency Controller (ARC) that proactively manages model weight residency and KV warmness to reduce cold-start-induced throughput drops while minimizing wasted GPU residency and memory pressure. ARC will coordinate with autoscaler and fleet controller to pre-stage weights, maintain soft-pinned residency tokens per-tenant/model, and prime tenant-specific KV caches using sampled traffic prefixes and lightweight synthetic queries.
acceptance_criteria: Fleet-wide warm-hit-rate for production tenants >= 92% during scale-up windows
Observed p99 token-generation overhead attributable to weight loading < 25ms for pinned models; < 150ms for fallback path during controlled spillovers
No >10% increase in GPU memory pressure on average across nodes after ARC enabled (measured over 24h)
Autoscaler-compatible plan that triggers pre-scale actions without causing oscillation (documented hysteresis parameters)
End-to-end rollout playbook and canary plan validated in staging with two pilot customers
success_metrics: Cold start events causing request-level retries — target <= 0.5%
Median extra latency due to weight/kv fetch during burst < 30ms
Cost delta (GPU-hours reserved for ARC policy) — target < +6% for typical fleets
design_notes: ARC runs as a control-plane agent co-located with fleet-autoscaler and exposes a small duty cycle worker on each node to accept residency tokens.
Forecasting: use short-horizon request-rate forecasts (10s-2m window) derived from route-level telemetry; fallback to TTL-based heuristics when forecasts are unavailable.

Residency tokens: lightweight leases assigned to model+tenant tuples. Soft pinning avoids hard replication for low-confidence forecasts; pins promote to hard residency when sustained traffic exceeds thresholds.
KV priming: seed top-k prefix keys based on sampled recent prefixes and optionally run synthetic warm queries that populate KV cache asynchronously with low priority.
Spillover policy: when memory pressure rises, evict soft-pinned models first, then least-recently-used tenants within a model shard. Provide configurable eviction windows to avoid oscillation.

Autoscaler integration: pre-scale GPU pool when aggregated forecasted qps per-GPU exceeds configured throughput-guarantee thresholds; ARC emits pre-stage requests to warm nodes during scale-up lead time.
Fallbacks: automatically route to quantized/compact model variants if residency cannot be achieved within a soft timeout. Customers can configure acceptable variant downgrade levels.
Observability: expose per-tenant warmness score, residency state transitions, forecast confidence, and memory pressure signals to Console for troubleshooting and SLA audits.
implementation_steps: Prototype residency token format and control-plane API (controller + node agent) — spike to evaluate overhead
Implement short-horizon forecasting service using existing telemetry ingestion (route-level qps and recent tokens) — reuse runtime histograms
Node agent: implement lightweight admission that accepts residency tokens, initiates weight load (with staged weight staging lanes) and KV priming job with priority gating
Autoscaler hooks: add pre-scale webhook and a pre-stage action that reserves GPU slots for expected load; ensure hysteresis params to avoid flapping
Telemetry plumbing: add metrics for warm-hit-rate, soft-vs-hard pinned counts, priming job success/failure, and memory pressure per-node
End-to-end tests in staging: synthetic burst tests, tenant churn simulations, and long-tail cold-start regressions
Canary rollout: 5% fleet -> 25% -> 100% with rollback triggers tied to warm-hit-rate and latency SLOs
Documentation: brief runbook, release notes, and Console dashboard updates
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-pinning increases memory pressure and evicts useful models — Mitigation: soft pins with time-decay and eviction priority configuration
Risk: Forecasting errors cause unnecessary pre-scaling and cost spike — Mitigation: conservative confidence threshold, budget cap per-fleet, and simulated dry-run mode for first 2 weeks

Risk: KV priming may return stale entries or cause privacy exposure for multi-tenant data — Mitigation: only prime read-only embedding/kv entries that are tenant-scoped and run under tenant ACLs; require security review for cross-tenant heuristics
Risk: Oscillation between ARC and autoscaler — Mitigation: introduce explicit handoff and hysteresis with cooldown windows and rate-limits on pre-stage actions

2026-03-08 Design review (Liam O'Sullivan): Suggested UX for Console to show per-tenant warmness and to expose a transparent explanation for eviction events.

notes_for_rollout: Start with non-critical fleets and two pilot customers. Enable ARC in dry-run mode initially (metrics-only) for 72h, then enable active pre-stage with conservative thresholds. Monitor warm-hit-rate, memory pressure, and autoscaler behavior closely. Rollback if warm-hit-rate drops or sustained memory pressure > 95th percentile threshold.
